verdict.rationale: Pixel-tracking protection and data transparency are fair questions for an email client, so the axis applies. However, no first-party evidence documents blocking read pixels by default or explaining how mail data is handled. Community reports say the opposite: users cannot turn images off, and Superhuman stores emails on its servers.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data
